record_note: This page records what the cited court records and reports say happened. Findings belong to the court or authority that made them; this register adds none of its own. Names of private individuals are withheld unless a naming gate clears them.
landing_tail: Punished for exercising basic freedoms — freedom of speech, freedom of religion, and more sections to come.

records.date_label: Fifth arrest and remand (reports give 4 or 5 July)
records.title: YouTuber arrested five times in a week after a speech criticising the Deputy Chief Minister; anti-terror law added
records.authority: Andhra Pradesh Police (several districts); remanded by a court at Gannavaram
laws: Sections 13 and 39, Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967
Sections 147, 148, 152, 192, 197(1)(d) and 353(1)(b), Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
records.person: A Dalit Christian YouTuber and activist
records.summary: A YouTuber who criticised Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan at a Dalit Christian meeting in Eluru on 28 June 2026 was arrested five times in about a week by police in different districts, each time in a new case after the last one ended in bail or a refused remand. The fifth case, over a video posted in November 2025, added the anti-terror law UAPA, and a court remanded him to judicial custody until 18 July.
detail: News reports say the YouTuber spoke at a Dalit Christian meeting in Eluru in late June 2026, where he attacked ruling-party leaders over what he called inaction on atrocities against Dalits. IANS reported the date as 28 June and said the complaint concerned 'derogatory remarks' against Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan.

According to ThePrint, he was first taken into custody on 30 June by Kakinada district police. After bail he was arrested again on 2 July by Sarpavaram police in a pending 2025 case, then on 3 July by Machilipatnam and Inaguduru police, and on 4 July by Payakaraopeta police, when a court at Anakapalli rejected the remand request. IANS reported that he 'secured bail for the fourth time on July 4'.

He was then arrested a fifth time by Gannavaram police in Krishna district at the Vempadu toll plaza. Police invoked sections 13 and 39 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and several sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, including section 152 (acts endangering the sovereignty and integrity of India). ThePrint reported that police said a video he posted on 25 November 2025 was 'very provocative' and 'supported and encouraged banned organisations such as the Maoists', and that it showed pictures of Maoist leaders killed in encounters.

A court at Gannavaram remanded him to judicial custody until 18 July 2026, and he was lodged in Nellore Central Jail, according to the same reports. His wife told reporters that he 'spoke the very same language that Pawan Kalyan used'.
records.current_position: Remanded to judicial custody until 18 July 2026 in the UAPA case, according to news reports. We have not found a published court order or any later report on bail.

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: Speech, then a stack of cases
sections.text: The first arrest followed a political speech criticising a minister. The pattern that followed, a fresh arrest in a different district each time a court released him, ending in an anti-terror charge over a months-old video, is the kind of use of criminal process against speech this register documents. The courts have made no finding on the charges.

records.caveats: No court order in these cases has been published online yet, so this record rests on news reports (V1). Reports differ on whether the fifth arrest was on 4 or 5 July 2026. We do not know whether he has since been granted bail in the UAPA case.

records.date_label: Caste certificates cancelled by gazette notification
records.title: Pastor loses Scheduled Caste status for practising Christianity; his caste certificates are cancelled
records.authority: Supreme Court of India; District Collector, Bapatla
records.case_reference: Criminal Appeal No. 1580 of 2026, 2026 INSC 283 (from Crl.P. No. 7114 of 2022, High Court of Andhra Pradesh; FIR No. 08 of 2021, Chandole Police Station)
laws: Paragraph 3, Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950
Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 (protection held unavailable)
Andhra Pradesh (Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Backward Classes) Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates Act, 1993
acts: Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
Andhra Pradesh Regulation of Issue of Community Certificates Act, 1993
records.person: A pastor from Kothapalem village, Bapatla district
records.summary: A Dalit pastor who said he was assaulted and warned to stop holding Sunday prayer meetings lost the protection of the anti-atrocities law because he practises Christianity. On 24 March 2026 the Supreme Court held that conversion ends Scheduled Caste status 'from the moment of conversion'. On 23 May 2026 the Bapatla district collector cancelled his three caste certificates.
detail: The Supreme Court recorded that the appellant, from Kothapalem village in Pittalavanipalem mandal, belongs by birth to the Madiga community, a Scheduled Caste, and had for about ten years been conducting Sunday prayer meetings as a pastor in houses in the village.

He alleged that in January 2021 men from the village assaulted him, abused him by caste and 'warned him against continuing the prayer meetings'. Chandole police registered FIR No. 08 of 2021 under the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and the Indian Penal Code and filed a charge sheet.

On 30 April 2025 the High Court of Andhra Pradesh quashed the case, holding that a person who 'had been openly professing Christianity and working as a Pastor' cannot claim protection under the SC/ST Act. On 24 March 2026 a Supreme Court bench of Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Manmohan dismissed his appeal. It held that under paragraph 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950, only Hindus, Sikhs and Buddhists can be members of a Scheduled Caste, and that no statutory benefit or protection tied to caste status can be extended to anyone else.

News reports say that after the ruling a District Level Scrutiny Committee enquired into his caste status, and that on its recommendation the Bapatla District Collector cancelled three certificates issued to him (dated 15 March 2021, 22 October 2022 and 28 February 2025) with immediate effect, by an Extraordinary Gazette notification dated 23 May 2026.

The Supreme Court also agreed with the High Court that the investigation material did not support the assault and intimidation allegations. This record takes no view on those allegations; it concerns the holding that his religion alone removes his caste status.
records.current_position: Scheduled Caste status held lost by the Supreme Court (24 March 2026); caste certificates cancelled by the Bapatla district collector (gazette of 23 May 2026, as reported).

quote.heading: What the Supreme Court held
quote.text: No person who professes a religion other than Hindu, Sikh or Buddhist shall be deemed to be a member of a Scheduled Caste. This bar under Clause 3 of the Constitution (Scheduled Castes) Order, 1950 is categorical and absolute. Conversion to any religion not specified in Clause 3 results in immediate and complete loss of Scheduled Caste status from the moment of conversion regardless of birth.
quote.where: Supreme Court of India, 2026 INSC 283 (Criminal Appeal No. 1580 of 2026), conclusions (b)

sections.label: Why it is listed
sections.heading: A status that depends on faith
sections.text: A Hindu, Sikh or Buddhist of the same caste keeps Scheduled Caste status and the legal protections that go with it; a Christian or Muslim loses them. The pastor's certificates were cancelled because of the religion he practises, which makes this a penalty on professing a faith.

records.caveats: We have not located the 23 May 2026 gazette notification online; its details come from news reports that quote it. The Supreme Court judgment is the primary record.

records.title: Supreme Court quashes Gujarat FIR over MP's poem video posted in Jamnagar
records.summary: Police in Jamnagar registered an FIR against a Rajya Sabha member over a video with a poem posted on X. The Gujarat High Court refused to quash it in January 2025. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal on 28 March 2025 and quashed the FIR and all further proceedings.
records.case_reference: Criminal Appeal No. 1545 of 2025; FIR No. 11202008250014 of 2025, City A-Division Police Station, Jamnagar; R/Special Criminal Application (Quashing) No. 551 of 2025 (Gujarat High Court)
laws: Sections 196, 197(1), 302, 299, 57 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
records.person: a Rajya Sabha member who posted a video in Jamnagar, Gujarat
detail: The Supreme Court recorded that FIR No. 11202008250014 of 2025 was registered with City A-Division Police Station, Jamnagar for offences punishable under Sections 196, 197(1), 302, 299, 57 and 3(5) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023.

The Supreme Court recorded that the appellant had posted a 46-second video of a mass marriage gathering in Jamnagar on social media platform X from a verified account, with Urdu verses as background audio, and that the complainant claimed the clip stirred inter-group hostility.

Verdictum reported that the Gujarat High Court declined to quash the case on 17 January 2025 on the ground that investigation was at a nascent stage, that the Supreme Court stayed further steps on 21 January 2025, reserved verdict on 3 March 2025, and quashed the case on 28 March 2025.

Verdictum reported that the Supreme Court held no offence was attracted, that police must read the actual words when speech is involved, and that in a healthy democracy views must be countered with other views.
records.current_position: The FIR and all further proceedings stand quashed by the Supreme Court on 28 March 2025.

records.title: High Court quashes case over remarks about Prime Minister in Athani shop dispute
records.summary: Athani Police booked a shopkeeper after a social worker complained about barricades and alleged insulting remarks about the Prime Minister. The Karnataka High Court quashed the proceedings before the Athani court. The Court held the complaint did not show intentional insult to provoke a breach of peace.
records.authority: Karnataka High Court, Justice Venkatesh Naik T
laws: Section 285 BNS
Section 352 BNS
detail: The High Court recorded that Athani Police booked the petitioner after a complaint about barricades placed near his shop and alleged insulting remarks against the Prime Minister. LiveLaw reported the complaint was lodged on January 11, 2026 about a January 7, 2026 incident near the petitioner's shop, after a video circulated on a WhatsApp group.

The High Court recorded that the only allegation was a political statement against the Prime Minister, with no specific allegation that the petitioner abused or intentionally insulted the complainant. The petitioner's counsel argued a political statement could not be converted into a personal prosecution when basic ingredients were not met.

The High Court held that mere abuse, rudeness or insolence is not intentional insult without the requisite intention or knowledge to provoke breach of peace. LiveLaw reported the Court relied on [name withheld] v. State of U.P. (2023) in interpreting Sections 285 and 352 BNS.

The High Court noted a four-day delay in the complaint and called the allegations general and omnibus. The Court held continuation of proceedings would amount to abuse of process of law, and quashed the pending case before the Principal Civil Judge and JMFC, Athani.
records.current_position: The criminal proceedings before the Athani court stand quashed.

quote.text: The allegation against the petitioner is essentially that, when the complainant questioned him regarding the barricades, he made certain statements against the Hon'ble Prime Minister of India. There is no specific allegation that the petitioner abused or intentionally insulted the complainant so as to provoke a breach of peace..

records.title: High Court quashes anti-conversion FIR over pamphlets near Jamkhandi temple
records.summary: Police registered an anti-conversion case after three men distributed religious pamphlets and preached near a temple in Jamkhandi. The Karnataka High Court quashed the FIR and trial court proceedings. The Court held a third-party complainant had no standing and no specific conversion or attempt was alleged.
records.authority: Karnataka High Court, Dharwad Bench, Justice Venkatesh Naik T
laws: Sections 299, 351(2) and 3(5) BNS
Section 5 of the Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022
acts: Karnataka Protection of Right to Freedom of Religion Act, 2022
records.person: three men preaching near a temple in Jamkhandi
detail: LawBeat reported that on May 4, 2025 three men were found distributing religious pamphlets and preaching near the Ramatheerth Temple in Jamkhandi. A temple visitor complained they denounced other beliefs, claimed their mission was to spread their faith, and allegedly offered jobs and material benefits.

The High Court held the FIR was legally invalid because the complainant was an unrelated third party. Citizens for Justice and Peace reported the Court held only a converted person or close family, as listed in Section 4 of the 2022 Act, could complain.

The High Court held that even taking the FIR at face value, it did not show a concrete act of conversion or attempted conversion of any identifiable person. LawBeat reported the Court said preaching without coercion, allurement, fraud or misrepresentation does not attract the anti-conversion provisions.
The High Court quashed the FIR and all related proceedings before the Additional Civil Judge and JMFC Court, Jamkhandi.
records.current_position: The FIR and proceedings before the Jamkhandi court stand quashed.

records.caveats: Case number not printed in the reports consulted. District left null because only Jamkhandi is named on the pages opened. The FIR used the language of allurement, but the Court found no identifiable target or victim and no concrete attempt.

records.title: Pune court grants bail to party social-media chief held over posts about chief minister
records.summary: Police in the Pune region arrested a state social-media office-bearer in April 2026 over posts about the chief minister and government functioning. He was booked under BNS Section 152 among other sections. A Pune sessions court granted bail in July 2026, holding that criticism of the government alone is not waging war.
records.authority: Additional Sessions Judge [name withheld], Pune Sessions Court
laws: Section 152 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS)
records.person: state head of the social-media wing of a Maharashtra political party, based in Pune
detail: India Today reported that the Pune court granted bail to the office-bearer, saying criticism of the government or the chief minister by itself cannot be treated as waging war against the nation.

ThePrint, carrying PTI, reported that police had arrested the functionary in April on charges of circulating morphed photos of the Maharashtra chief minister and posting content allegedly sympathetic to Naxalites.

ThePrint reported that the court noted the case papers showed the applicant had questioned the investigation process in certain cases and the functioning of government schemes, which it said fell within the realm of public discourse.

India Today reported that the court said the investigation was over, the chargesheet had been filed, and no further custodial interrogation was required, and directed release on a personal bond of Rs 25,000 with one or two sureties.

ThePrint reported that the defence argued the case was politically motivated and protected speech, while the prosecution opposed bail saying objectionable language and offences against the State were involved.
records.current_position: Released on bail; chargesheet filed and investigation complete, prosecution pending trial with conditions not to tamper with evidence and not to leave the country without permission.

records.title: Orissa High Court refuses pre-arrest bail to news editor booked over video remarks about minister
records.summary: Capital Police in Bhubaneswar booked the editor-in-chief of a digital news platform after a video of his remarks about a State minister was widely circulated on social media. The editor sought pre-arrest bail, saying custodial interrogation was not needed. The Orissa High Court rejected the plea on 6 August 2026 and left the prosecution pending.
records.authority: Orissa High Court (Justice V. Narasingh); Capital Police, Bhubaneswar
records.case_reference: Capital P.S. Case No.561 of 2026; C.T. Case No.1736 of 2026 (SDJM, Bhubaneswar); ABLAPL No.8997 of 2026
laws: Section 353 BNS
Section 196 BNS
Section 356 BNS
records.person: editor-in-chief of a digital news platform in Bhubaneswar
detail: The High Court recorded that the case arose from remarks made during an Odisha Swabhiman Mancha programme on 12.07.2026, where the editor claimed a State minister had tried to bribe him to suppress reports about textbook errors, and that a video of the claim was uploaded and widely circulated on Facebook and other social media platforms.

Police said the complaint described the statements as false, fabricated, malicious and defamatory, published to tarnish the minister's reputation, mislead the public and disturb public order and confidence in the government, and registered Capital PS case no. 561 dated 14.07.2026 under Sections 353, 196 and 356 BNS.

The editor told the High Court that even taking the allegations at face value, custodial interrogation was not warranted, that his listed criminal antecedents were irrelevant, and that co-accused persons taken into custody had been released on bail.

The State opposed bail by citing materials on record including the Section 183 BNSS statement of a correspondent working under the editor, and by placing a list of 20 prior criminal cases across police stations between 2022 and 2026 before the Court.

Justice V. Narasingh held that the materials did not warrant the exceptional remedy of pre-arrest bail, rejected the application, and clarified that the observations were only for the bail plea and that the accusation had to be established independently in the ongoing probe.
records.current_position: Pre-arrest bail stands rejected and the criminal case before the SDJM, Bhubaneswar remains pending investigation.

quote.text: Considering the materials on record and perusal of the statement of the correspondent, who works under the Petitioner, recorded under Section 183 of BNSS and other statements, this Court is not inclined to entertain the application of the Petitioner for grant of “exceptional remedy” of pre-arrest bail. The same accordingly stands rejected.

records.caveats: Full FIR and case diary were not opened; the State's list of 20 prior cases could not be independently verified; later bail or arrest developments after 6 August 2026 were not confirmed.

records.title: Chennai commentator booked over temple-land posts, High Court quashes cybercrime FIR
records.summary: Chennai cybercrime police registered an FIR over posts linking the State Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Minister to a temple-land registration. The Madras High Court quashed the FIR on 28 August 2026, holding the cited public-order offences were not made out.
records.authority: Madras High Court; Chennai Central Crime Branch, Cyber Cell CCD-I

detail: The High Court recorded that the complaint was given by the junior personal assistant of the State Hindu Religious and Charitable Endowments Minister, alleging wilful malicious disinformation on X and Instagram about fraudulent registration of land of a Palani temple.
Police registered Crime No. 82 of 2026 for offences under Sections 192, 353(1)(b) and 353(2) of the BNS.

The High Court held that no rioting was intended or occurred, and the posts were not shown to promote enmity on religion or community grounds, so none of the three charged offences was made out even if allegations were taken at face value.

The High Court quashed the FIR but left it open to the minister or complainant to pursue civil or criminal defamation, and directed the commentator to file an affidavit expressing regret for an unverified post and undertaking future verification.

records.title: Thiruvarur prayer house ordered shut and sealed over meetings without permission
records.summary: The Kodavasal Tahsildar ordered a pastor-run trust to close a prayer house within 10 days and the premises were sealed after a police enquiry. The pastor challenged the closure in the Madras High Court. On 13 June 2025 the Court ordered desealing for possession but barred use as a prayer hall without District Collector permission.
records.authority: Tahsildar, Kodavasal Taluk; District Collector, Thiruvarur; Madras High Court
records.case_reference: W.P. No. 2036 of 2024; impugned proceedings No. Pa.Ve.01/2023/A5 dated 20.01.2024

records.person: a pastor running a Christian trust in Kodavasal Taluk, Thiruvarur district
records.penalty: Closure notice and seal on prayer premises; continued bar on use as prayer hall without permission
detail: The High Court recorded that the pastor ran a trust established in 2007 and held regular prayer meetings with relatives and neighbours on property purchased in January 2023.

The High Court recorded that after a complaint, the Kodavasal police held an enquiry, building permission for a church was rejected, and the Tahsildar issued a notice directing closure of the prayer house within 10 days failing which action would follow.
The District Collector said, according to the judgment, that a prayer hall could not be run without proper permission and that meetings caused disturbance to neighbours.
The High Court held that a house cannot as a matter of right be used as a prayer hall for large congregations without permission, and that the undertaking to avoid loudspeakers was insufficient.
The High Court directed removal of the seal to restore possession but barred use as a prayer hall without permission and left it open to authorities to proceed in accordance with law on reuse.
records.current_position: The seal is to be removed for possession, but the premises must not be used as a prayer hall without District Collector permission.

quote.text: The property shall not be utilised as a prayer hall for conducting prayer meetings and if the petitioner intends to convert the property into a prayer hall, the petitioner is directed to approach the District Collector and seek for permission.
quote.where: Pastor [name withheld] v District Collector, W.P. No. 2036 of 2024, Madras High Court judgment dated 13.06.2025, para 9

records.caveats: No 2026 official record of punishment for peaceful worship alone was found; neighbour disturbance was alleged by the Collector but no violence, force or fraud finding was made. Exact sealing date beyond the January 2024 notice was not stated in the judgment.
